name: Skin
description: Skin (or 'Georgia Skin') is a legendary high-stakes gambling game from the American South. It is a banking game, but not in the traditional sense where the bank has an edge; the edge comes purely from chance, nerve, and 'side bets'. Cards are dealt from a shoe one by one. Players bet on their card being matched by a card from the deck. If your card is matched (falls), you lose. The last card standing ('The Skin') is the winner unless all bets are resolved earlier. It is famous for its slow, tension-filled reveal ('Skinning').
deck: Standard 52-card deck (often multiple decks in a shoe for large games)

history.origins: Developed in the 19th century among African American communities in the South, likely derived from Faro. It was notorious in juke joints and turpentine camps.
timeline: 1920s: Recorded by blues musicians (e.g., 'Skin Game Blues' by Peg Leg Howell).
1940s: Mentioned in Zora Neale Hurston's folklore collections.
1970s: Fades from public eye but remains underground.
history.cultural: Known as the fairest gambling game because the house has zero mathematical edge (except a small rake if organized).
history.evolution: The term 'Skinning' refers to sliding the cards slowly from the shoe to build suspense.

setup.players: Two or more players; Scarne describes it as best for about six. One player is the banker (dealer). The first banker is chosen by dealing cards one at a time until an Ace appears; the turn to be banker passes to the right after each deal. Each player may accept one case card from the dealer to bet on, or refuse; the dealer also holds one card. Cards are revealed one by one from a dealing box or shoe.
setup.dealing: Players buy a card from the dealer (the 'Case Card'). Dealer takes a card too.

rules.objective: Have your card survive while others fall (are matched).
rules.gameplay: Players buy a case card from the dealer; the dealer also takes a card. Cards are then revealed one by one from the shoe. When a revealed card matches a player's card (same rank), that player is eliminated. The last card remaining wins unless all bets are resolved earlier. Side bets are common.
keyRules: Each player buys one case card from the dealer; the dealer takes one.
Cards are revealed one by one from the shoe (skinning).
When a revealed card matches your card's rank, you are eliminated.
The last card standing (The Skin) wins unless all bets are resolved earlier.
Side bets between players are common.

strategy.basic: Pure luck. There is no strategy in card selection since it's random. The strategy is in money management and reading opponents for side bets. If you see two 7s already gone, betting heavily on a 7 is safer (only one 7 left means less chance of falling soon? No, wait. If 2 7s are gone, there are 2 left in deck. Probability of falling is lower than if 3 were left? Yes. But eventually it must fall if you play to end of deck).
strategy.intermediate: The 'Turn': Watch the turn cards. If a card hasn't appeared for a long time (is 'sleeping'), it's due. Gambler's fallacy, but common in Skin logic.
strategy.advanced: Bankroll Management: In a fair game, variance will kill you. Don't bet everything on one card. Spread bets across multiple cards if allowed (playing two hands).
